title: OpenAI says slowing frontier AI may be necessary
content: Reuters reports Sam Altman told staff OpenAI is open to slowing AI development; OpenAI's September 9 policy statement says safety should set the pace when safeguards fall behind.

title: AI-safety alarm reaches Congress
content: Reuters and Axios report growing congressional concern after warnings from Anthropic researchers, with lawmakers calling for stronger oversight and new AI rules.

title: OpenAI asks for mandatory national AI-safety regulation
content: OpenAI is publicly advocating capability-based national safety requirements, independent assessment infrastructure and rules for when frontier development should slow or stop.

title: Nvidia targets up to 2 GW of Australian AI-factory capacity by 2027
content: Reuters reports Nvidia and Australian partners plan a large expansion of AI data-centre capacity, potentially adding up to 2 GW by 2027.

title: Google commits about $15B to Finnish AI infrastructure and nuclear power
content: Google announced a €13B investment in Finnish AI/digital infrastructure and a long-term nuclear power agreement, making compute and energy one combined strategic story.

title: OpenAI expands AI into chip design with Jalapeño
content: OpenAI says its own models accelerated the design and optimization of its Jalapeño inference chip, including a nine-month tape-out and later performance work.

title: Meta launches Muse, its proactive personal AI agent
content: Meta launched Muse as a personal agent that can proactively work on goals and take actions across connected services inside a dedicated secure VM.

title: DeepSeek starts preparing for a Shanghai STAR Market IPO
content: Reuters reports DeepSeek tapped CITIC Securities to prepare for a domestic STAR Market listing as compute and talent costs intensify.

title: Anthropic reports disrupting Russian and Chinese campaigns abusing Claude
content: Anthropic's September threat report details disrupted misuse across cyber, surveillance, weapons research and illicit distillation, while Reuters reports on Russian and Chinese-linked activity.

title: OpenAI–New York Times becomes a major fair-use test
content: The litigation is emerging as a key legal test of whether copyrighted material can lawfully be used for AI training under fair-use theories.
